body.statement:
Working over the baseline event-transfer slices
\(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), use the second-order staircase alignment
handle to derive a primitive block-ratio expression
\(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants
\(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that
\[
 c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
 \le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 \le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
\]
for every vanishing \(\eta_n\).  The upper-band implication is expressly
conditional on the unresolved feasible-score premise: there must exist
\(h_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
Under that premise, prove that
\(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) implies
\(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\).

Conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with
\(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^\dagger\) and
\(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which
\(\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero,
construct one complete selected pair in the common subclass
\(\mathfrak M^\cap\).  Its law coordinates must satisfy
\[
 \delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n),
 \qquad \liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0,
\]
and the witness itself must establish feasible-score stability for some
\(h_n\downarrow0\):
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
The derivation must first compute whether the balanced strong-factor
rank-one second-order remainder is
\(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so,
\(\Delta^\dagger\) must use the smaller attained scale.  Because the
published class permits \(M^R\ne0\), no upper-band conclusion is requested
for its full projection without an additional approximation-bias remainder.

obligation.what_is_open: Compute the exact signed second-order remainder of the specified Choi--Yuan estimator on a balanced rank-one complete array in \(\mathfrak M^\cap\), determine whether it is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\), and prove both an attained \(1-\eta_n\) quantile lower bound and feasible-score stability for the same counterarray.
obligation.obstruction: Proposition A.4 supplies an upper perturbation envelope after several norm inequalities, not an attained expansion.  The frozen estimator construction names the nuclear-norm and debiasing procedure but does not specify its tuning rule, KKT solution, or signed second-order map.  First-order coefficients and the two-horizon covariance witness therefore do not determine the nonlinear remainder or its sign.  The frozen assumptions also contain no rowwise loading rate for the leave-one-cell-out feasible score.
obligation.attempted: The class-scope obstruction was removed: the published model was encoded as an array plus one selected functional, the actual event-block correspondence was stated, and a balanced rank-one array was shown by direct rate substitution to lie in a nonempty common subclass.  On that array the primitive ratios, leverage, marginal scale, and published six hypotheses were computed.  These calculations still leave the estimator's second-order KKT remainder unidentified, so neither a reverse perturbation inequality nor undercoverage can be inferred from the first-order witness.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact nonprimitive frontier remains identified by the definitions:
\[
 \Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 =\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 \inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}.
\]
For any \(u_n\) satisfying
\(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\le\eta_n\), the generic transfer theorem
gives a computable coverage bound after adding the displayed uniform
feasible-score premise.  In the i.i.d. homoskedastic source submodel,
\(\texttt{thm:uniform-influence}\) further gives
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq
 \mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)),
\]
and hence the one-sided quantile bound
\(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) whenever the
unsimplified source union bound is at most \(\eta_n\).  This does not give
a uniform upper bound over the whole baseline event-transfer slice.
The explicit balanced rank-one construction in
\(\texttt{prop:published-class-comparison}\) proves that the corrected
common subclass is nonempty and verifies both distinct families of rate
conditions.  It does not determine the nonlinear remainder: the frozen
construction of \(\widehat M^0\) omits the tuning rule, KKT solution, and
signed second-order debiasing expansion needed to compute its attained
quantile.  No reverse inequality, sign-aligned counterarray, or feasible
score rate for that counterarray has therefore been proved.

body.justification: The remaining mathematical question is panel-specific attainability of the signed second-order remainder, not generic Gaussian approximation.
body.gap: No source or frozen construction gives the exact KKT remainder, an aligned lower bound, or feasible-score stability for the same counterarray.
body.consumer: Resolution would determine whether the primitive Choi--Yuan envelope is sharp or can be replaced by a smaller attained scale without overstating feasible coverage.
